solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Space traveller leaves

definitions.meaning: a craft propelled into orbit or beyond by burning fuel
the peppery salad leaf also called arugula

explanation.surface: Someone journeying through space takes off and departs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spacecraft launcher and a salad green, so each stretch of the clue is a full synonym.

clue.text: Stop working and hit the sack

definitions.meaning: to give up employment for good, at the end of a career
an idiom meaning go to bed

explanation.surface: Finishing work and heading to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers leaving one's career and also going to bed for the night.

clue.text: Warm, fruit-flavoured drink

definitions.meaning: warm here means friendly and heartfelt
a sweet concentrated fruit syrup diluted with water

explanation.surface: A hot fruity beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means genially friendly and also names a diluted fruit squash.

clue.text: Bird found in better neighbourhood

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words better neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A bird lives in a nicer part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a crossword-favourite bird.

clue.text: Proust novel in state of unconsciousness

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of the author's name are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A Proust novel sends its reader into a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun, a book by Proust, but it is the anagram signal working as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A daze or near-insensible condition is a synonym for a stunned, senseless state.

clue.text: Eccentric in act, yet to show persistence

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Odd behaviour in a play that nevertheless shows determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged determination to keep going is a synonym for persistence.

clue.text: Pulp has gone over the top of everything

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: something that has gone is past

indicators.note: the top of means the first letter of the word everything, top being first in a down clue

explanation.surface: A mushy mess has spilled over everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft moist mass, such as tomato concentrate, is a kind of pulp.

clue.text: Greatly enjoy sauce

definitions.meaning: a condiment such as a pickle or chutney

explanation.surface: Really loving a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for enjoying keenly and a noun for a tangy condiment.

clue.text: US state I saw under bridge

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the remaining pieces sit below the bridge

parts.note: to bridge two things is to connect them
to saw is to cut

explanation.surface: A traveller spotting a US state from below a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see but is the cutting tool's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The New England state with Hartford as capital is one of the fifty in America.

clue.text: Hill over Canadian city

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
onto, as in climbing over and on to something

explanation.surface: Crossing a hill to reach a city in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario's capital is the largest urban centre in Canada.

clue.text: Primarily, noses always sound, appropriately, like — this?

definitions.text: Primarily, noses always sound, appropriately, like — this?

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A musing on how noses make their sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the opening letters spell the word for a voice that comes through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound produced through the nose is described with this adjective, fitting the 'like this' of the clue.

clue.text: Track fibber on the way back

indicators.note: travelling back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a fibber is a liar

explanation.surface: Following the trail of a fibber as he returns.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway line is a track, so a single bar of it is a synonym.

clue.text: Thieves after a thousand items of underwear

indicators.note: after means the thieves come behind the thousand in the answer

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for a thousand, from kilo
to nick is British slang for to steal, so nickers are thieves

explanation.surface: Burglars chasing a big haul of lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: British English uses this word for women's briefs or panties.

clue.text: Dire stew cooked up, most odd

indicators.note: cooked up means concocted, so the letters are prepared in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A terrible stew is the strangest dish yet.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of strange, most peculiar, matches most odd.

clue.text: Rounding first of chairs, change row

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the change surrounds the chosen letter

parts.note: an alteration is a change

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of the word chairs

explanation.surface: A meeting row breaks out over who sits where after a change of chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' here, a quarrel, not a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy quarrel or heated dispute is a synonym for a row.

clue.text: Where butter may be found in the groove

definitions.meaning: an idiom for enjoying a run of success

explanation.surface: Where to look for butter when things go well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places butter on bread and idiomatically means enjoying a winning streak.

clue.text: European run taking in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: taking in means the run holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a dash is a short run

explanation.surface: A continental traveller on a jaunt through Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Denmark is a Scandinavian, and so a European.

clue.text: Misdeed on a European peninsula

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a misdeed is a crime

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing committed on a European peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea landmass jutting from Ukraine is a peninsula in Europe.

clue.text: A bodybuilder — one's out of this world!

parts.note: a steroid is a drug that builds body muscle

explanation.surface: Praising a muscleman as extraordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bodybuilder' seems to be a gym-goer but is the drug that builds bodies; 'out of this world' is taken literally, a body in space.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky minor planet orbiting the sun is literally something not of our world.

clue.text: Jewelled item found in Croatia rarely

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words Croatia rarely

explanation.surface: Jewellery seldom turns up in Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem-set crown or headband is a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Just blonde

definitions.meaning: blonde means light-coloured, of hair or complexion

explanation.surface: Simply blonde.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both even-handed and pale-haired, matching each definition as a synonym.

clue.text: A drink knocked up in Tuscan city

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A drink whipped up in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of the Leaning Tower lies in the Italian region of Tuscany.

clue.text: One ahead of pace, incensed

indicators.note: ahead of means the one comes before the pace in the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
pace means speed or rate

explanation.surface: Furious at being first ahead of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very angry or furious is a synonym for incensed.

clue.text: Always the same, educational document?

parts.note: uni, short for university, is a place of education
a form is a document to be filled in

explanation.surface: A school paper that never varies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant and unvarying throughout is a synonym for always the same.

clue.text: English county filing a suit

indicators.note: filing means moving in a line, so the letter goes in and lies inside the county

parts.note: Herts is the abbreviation for Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: Someone in an English county lodging a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks legal but is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four sets in a pack of playing cards, with red symbols, is a suit.

clue.text: Spanish food bringing father and girl together

indicators.note: bringing, with together later in the clue, says the pieces are joined
bringing the two together means the two pieces are joined side by side

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish meal unites dad and daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Valencian rice dish with saffron and seafood is a classic food from Spain.
